comment: Echowire: the one description of who may see a thread, read by two implementations.
fluxer_api/src/api/channel/services/ThreadAccess.ts decides it for the HTTP api, and
Both are exercised against this file, so the two cannot drift apart silently:
parent_permissions lists the caller's permissions on the PARENT channel, already resolved.
Only two bits matter to the thread rules, so only two names are used.
A case with parent_missing means the parent channel row is gone, which is the orphan rule.
expect_can_view is the single outcome both implementations must agree on.

cases.name: public thread inherits a parent that allows viewing
public thread inherits a parent that denies viewing
private thread hides from a non member without manage channels
private thread admits a manager who is not a member
private thread member still needs view on the parent
private thread manager still needs view on the parent
public thread with a deleted parent is viewable by nobody
private thread with a deleted parent is viewable by nobody, member or not
